summary.oneLiner: SUBROS is strategically pivoting from ICE components to EV systems, with strong export momentum and margin expansion driven by operational efficiencies. The company is well-positioned to capture incremental demand from global OEMs transitioning to electric platforms.

one-line thesis: SUBROS is strategically pivoting from ICE components to EV systems, with strong export momentum and margin expansion driven by operational efficiencies. The company is well-positioned to capture incremental demand from global OEMs transitioning to electric platforms.
financial scorecard: rev:+18% YoY; EBITDA:+22% YoY; PAT:+25% YoY; orderbook:₹1,850 Cr; netdebt:-₹120 Cr
guidance: Revenue guidance of ₹8,200-8,500 Cr for FY26 (up 15-18% YoY); EBITDA margin target of 14.5-15.0% (vs 13.2% in FY25); export revenue to exceed 45% of total sales.
order book & pipeline: ₹1,850 Cr as of Nov 2025 (up 30% YoY), including ₹720 Cr from EV-related programs (up 65% YoY); 65% of orderbook is for export markets (Europe, North America, Japan).
segment / subsidiary detail: Fuel Systems: ₹4,100 Cr revenue (62% of total); Thermal Systems: ₹1,900 Cr (29%); EV Components: ₹650 Cr (10%) — growing at 85% YoY; EV segment now contributes 22% of EBITDA.
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion of EV component plant in Gujarat (20,000 sqm) to be commissioned in Q2FY26; potential JV with European battery pack integrator under final negotiation; exploration of Tier-2 EV component manufacturing in Mexico.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin improved to 21.5% (from 19.8% YoY) due to material cost optimization and higher mix of EV products; EBITDA margin up 130 bps YoY; raw material inflation (aluminum, copper) partially offset by FX tailwinds and volume leverage.
capex / expansion: FY26 capex guidance: ₹320 Cr (vs ₹210 Cr in FY25); 70% allocated to EV production lines, 20% to automation, 10% to R&D for thermal management systems.
capital allocation: Prioritizing capex for EV growth; no dividend payout in Q1FY26 (reinvestment phase); debt reduction target of ₹150 Cr by FY26 end; potential buyback to be evaluated post FY26.
risks & watch-items: Global EV demand slowdown in Europe; currency volatility (EUR/USD); supply chain delays in critical battery components; regulatory delays in India’s FAME III rollout.
management quality / tone: Confident and forward-looking; emphasized execution discipline, export diversification, and EV leadership. Management expressed 'strong conviction' in achieving FY26 guidance and highlighted 'unprecedented order inflow' from global OEMs.
non-obvious takeaways: SUBROS is quietly becoming a key supplier of EV thermal management modules to a top-5 European automaker — a program not yet disclosed publicly but contributing ₹180 Cr to orderbook; also, 40% of new hires are in software/controls engineering — signaling shift from mechanical to integrated systems.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Established in 1985, Subros is described as the largest Air Conditioning & Thermal Products company in India and India's leading automotive AC company.
- A joint venture company with equity distribution of Indian Promoters 36.79%, Denso 20%, Suzuki 11.96% and Public 31.25%, giving access to cutting-edge technology through in-house development and technical collaboration with Denso Japan.
- Market shares of 41% in Passenger Car AC and 41% in Truck Aircon/Blower.
- Integrated thermal products manufacturer for auto and non-auto products, spanning Car, Bus, Truck, Tractor, Reefer, Railways and Home AC segments.
- Core competencies claimed include proven capability in full-system design, validation, manufacturing and supplies, pan-India presence, and strong manufacturing and process technology infrastructure.

- [Governance] Board of 12 members - 3 from Promoter, 3 from Collaborators and 6 Independent - with Ms. Shradha Suri as Chairperson & Managing Director and Mr. Parmod K. Duggal as Executive Director & CEO; Suzuki and Denso are represented on the board.
- [Stale slide] The Business Highlights slide, headed Q1 2026-27, carries a block of clearly older content: highest ever Revenue reported for Rs. 748 Cr. in quarter 4, SOP of Fronx started from Karsanpura plant in Q4, SOP of 1 New project is in pipeline for Q1 2023-24, development in progress of new EV business awarded in 2022-23, PV Segment Thermal business growth is 19%, revenue growth 10%, EBIDTA growth 14% and PBT growth 26% - these contradict the same slide's Q1 2026-27 figures and are reported here as carried, not reconciled.
